newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up on foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed higher on Monday, supported by foreing buying of plantation and food and beverage stocks, brokers said.

The all share index closed 2.8 points up at 844.1, with price gains outnumbering declines by 45 to 26. Aitken Spence & Co rose three rupees to 223, Diesel & Motor Engineering five to 60, Hayleys five to 280.
"Investors are buying in anticipation of good results to June, because the ones that have come so far have been exceptional," said Buddhike Payoe of Lanka Securitites.
Colombo stocks have risen over 23 points in the last six days, due to good corporate growth for the period to June, brokers said.
Turnover was 162.7 million, led by foreign buying of 949,900 Bogawantalawa Plantations, 385,900 Ceylon Brewery and 626,400 Kelani Valley Plantations shares, brokers said.
Foreign buying was worth 115.7 million rupees while selling was worth 105.3 million.
